cl_bup_other_opioids.q: Does Suboxone block other opioids, and for how long?
cl_bup_other_opioids.short: Only partly. In small lab studies, even high doses didn't fully block heroin or another opioid. After the last dose, its hold on opioid receptors faded slowly over 3 days of scans.
cl_bup_other_opioids.but: Each study had 3 to 10 volunteers on heroin, not in treatment. Fentanyl and overdose weren't studied.
how: In brain scans of people dependent on heroin, buprenorphine (Suboxone's main drug) took up more opioid receptors as the daily dose went up. At 16 mg a day, 9 to 20 in 100 were still free 4 hours after a dose.
Even at the highest doses tested, heroin and another opioid still had some effect. The review mentions people who take more of them to get past the block, but has no data on what happens then.
After 10 volunteers stopped 16 mg a day, free receptors rose from about 13 to 25 in 100 at 4 hours to about 75 to 90 in 100 at 3 days. These figures come from curves drawn between 4 scans.
The review's summary gives receptor levels needed to block other opioids. But its own authors say nobody knows them. A full block was never reliably seen.
cl_bup_other_opioids.rate: One review by the researchers who ran the studies, each with 3 to 10 volunteers, mostly men, all dependent on heroin. Receptor scans don't measure overdose risk, and fentanyl wasn't studied.

cl_bup_fentanyl_withdrawal.q: Can Suboxone put you in withdrawal if you use fentanyl?
cl_bup_fentanyl_withdrawal.short: Many say so. In a US survey, 37 in 100 who took Suboxone's main drug after fentanyl remembered severe withdrawal. After methadone, 15 in 100 did.
cl_bup_fentanyl_withdrawal.but: These are memories, not records. And the survey couldn't tell if Suboxone caused the withdrawal or just didn't ease it.
how: 1,163 people starting treatment at 49 US centres said they'd used fentanyl. 685 had taken buprenorphine, Suboxone's main drug, within a month after fentanyl. 250 of them remembered severe withdrawal.

The shorter the shortest wait they reported after fentanyl, the more often they remembered it: about 45 in 100 under a day, 34 in 100 at 1 to 2 days, about 25 in 100 at 2 days to a week, 14 in 100 at a week to a month. There was no clear cut-off.
The paper's summary says 22 in 100 for those who waited under a day. That's out of all 685 people. Out of the 339 who waited under a day, it's 45 in 100.
Nothing else that differed between people was taken into account. The dose, the form and who gave it weren't asked.
cl_bup_fentanyl_withdrawal.rate: One survey of what people remembered when they started treatment, with nothing else taken into account. Its one question couldn't separate withdrawal buprenorphine caused from withdrawal it didn't relieve.

cl_bup_after_stopping.short: In US records, about 5 in 100 people had an overdose treated by a doctor within 6 months of stopping. Nearly half went to an emergency department.
cl_bup_after_stopping.but: People who died were left out, so fatal overdoses aren't counted. And nobody stayed on Suboxone to compare with.
how: US public health insurance (Medicaid) records tracked 8,996 people for 6 months after they stopped Suboxone's main drug, buprenorphine. They'd been on it for 6 to 18 months.

464 had at least one overdose treated by a doctor (5 in 100). 41 to 49 in 100 went to an emergency department, 11 to 14 in 100 stayed in hospital and 19 to 26 in 100 filled a prescription for another opioid.
People who'd been on it 15 to 18 months had fewer emergency visits, hospital stays and opioid prescriptions afterwards than those who stopped at 6 to 9 months. Their overdoses were no fewer.
Anyone who died or lost Medicaid in those 6 months was left out, and the records don't say why people stopped. Deaths during and after treatment are in a separate answer.
cl_bup_after_stopping.rate: One large study of insurance records. But people who died were left out, overdoses counted only if a doctor billed for them, and nobody who stayed on treatment was there to compare with.

methadone-buprenorphine.statement: Scientists know just how much Suboxone it takes to block other opioids.
methadone-buprenorphine.why: The researchers behind the brain scans say nobody knows. The levels in their summary came from early modelling of a few volunteers.

methadone-buprenorphine.statement: In one US study, about 5 in 100 had a doctor treat an overdose within 6 months of stopping Suboxone.
methadone-buprenorphine.why: 464 of 8,996 people on Medicaid who stopped after 6 to 18 months did. People who died were left out, so fatal overdoses aren't counted.

heroin.statement: People who stayed on Suboxone longer had fewer overdoses after they stopped.
heroin.why: In one large US study, about 5 in 100 had an overdose treated by a doctor, whether they'd been on it 6 or 18 months. A small difference could have been missed.

fentanyl-and-analogues.statement: In a US survey, over 1 in 3 people who took buprenorphine (as in Suboxone) after fentanyl remembered severe withdrawal.
fentanyl-and-analogues.why: 250 of 685 did (37 in 100), against 15 in 100 after methadone. These were memories, and the survey couldn't tell withdrawal buprenorphine caused from withdrawal it didn't ease.
